place: UNIDENTIFIED granite village centre in interior north-central Portugal, most likely Beira Alta (Guarda district plateau: Trancoso / Celorico da Beira / Fornos de Algodres / Aguiar da Beira area). Camera stands on cobbled granite setts beside a detached square granite bell tower built on a mossy granite boulder, next to a granite churchyard/precinct wall with an iron gate topped by a stone cross and pyramidal ball pinnacles, and a long whitewashed building with granite cornice and small high square windows.
evidence: Text: 'VENDE-SE [phone redacted]' (PT mobile) with a second number starting [French +33 number, redacted] (French prefix -> emigrant owner, typical of Beira Interior / Tras-os-Montes); manhole cover 'SANEAMENTO'; PT-style 'sem saida' (dead-end) sign; Peugeot 206 with an unreadable plate

Architecture: granite-sett streets with granite outcrops breaking through the paving; casa beira with a covered alpendre on a single granite column over a massive granite lintel and ground-floor lojas with green mesh doors; mixed rubble/ashlar granite houses

Church complex: detached square ashlar bell tower with corner pilasters, mid-height cornice, upper stage with one grilled rectangular opening, low hipped tiled roof with corner ball finials and an iron cross, standing on a large granite boulder; granite precinct wall with a gate under a stone cross flanked by pyramidal pinnacles with balls (17th-18th c. Beira style); behind it a granite church roof with pinnacles

Sun: overcast; brightest sky region at yaw ~+52 (pitch ~36, cloud glow; true sun elevation at 12:08 UTC/local on 13 Dec at 40.5N is ~26 deg, azimuth ~174) -> yaw 0 ~ bearing 122 +/- 20 deg (camera clock = local time in December, UTC+0)

Ruled out by comparing photos: Mata de Lobos, Sortelha (belfry is a bell gable on the wall), Sernancelhe, Belmonte, Castelo Mendo, Castelo Rodrigo, Penela da Beira, Penedono, Meda, Fonte Arcada, Pinhel, Almeida, Mogadouro, Retaxo, Pero Viseu, Caria, Poiares (Freixo; schist), Sarzedas (schist), Folgosinho, Celorico da Beira matriz; plus satellite thumbnails of 93 OSM bell towers that sit just outside a church outline with the church to their S
method: No exact fix. Region from architecture/materials/emigration clue; heading from the sun glow only. Identification attempts: web search (PT phrasings for detached bell tower on a boulder), Wikimedia Commons categories and a 19,570-file geosearch grid over Beira Alta (40.05-41.30N, 8.15-6.80W) filtered for tower/bell titles, OSM Overpass (762 bell towers + 11,209 church outlines N/Central PT; clock towers), Wikidata. The tower is apparently neither mapped as a separate OSM bell tower nor photographed under a findable Commons title. Next step for a human: search the SIPA inventory or Google Street View/Mapillary for 'torre sineira' + 'penedo' in Guarda/Viseu villages, or ask the team (MCQ) for the district.
